Class Toml

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.toml.Toml
public final class Toml extends Object
Parses and writes TOML 1.1 documents. 
TomlTable config = Toml.parse(file).root();
int port = config.getInt("server.port");

Toml.write(config, CharSink.of(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

The parser accepts every valid TOML 1.1 document, and rejects every invalid one with a TomlParseException. A document may start with a byte order mark, which is ignored. A parsed TomlDocument also tells where each of its keys and values is written, through its TomlPositions.

The writer writes the entries of a table before its subtables, and keeps the order of each. It writes nothing but the data: comments, blank lines and the choice between equivalent notations, such as a literal string or a dotted key, are not kept from a parsed document. It writes newlines as \n, and only TOML 1.0 notation, so that TOML 1.0 parsers can read what it writes too.

Since:
0.1.0

    • toTable

      public static TomlTable toTable(Record value)
      Converts a TomlConfig record to a table, which binds back to an equal record.

      Each component is the value of its key, in the form that TomlConfig binds: a Duration in ISO-8601, such as "PT1M30S"; a Path or a URI as its toString(); an enum as the key of its constant; a list or a set as an array, in its iteration order; a map or a record as a table. A null @Nullable component is left out.

      Parameters:
      value - the record
      Returns:
      the table
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if no TomlBinder is registered for the class of value, or if a string in it contains an unpaired surrogate
      NullPointerException - if value is null, or a value in it that is not @Nullable

    • writeAtomically

      public static void writeAtomically(TomlTable table, Path file) throws IOException
      Writes a table as a UTF-8 document to a file, atomically: readers, or the next run after a crash, see either the previous content of the file or the whole document, never a part of it. The file keeps its permissions.
      Parameters:
      table - the root table of the document
      file - the file to create or replace
      Throws:
      IOException - if writing the file fails, which leaves it as it was
      NullPointerException - if table or file is null
      See Also:
      • AtomicFiles.write(Path, AtomicFiles.Output)
